derivations.quote: Both $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B_0$ are contractions, each applied one line (entries along one axis) at a time in a padded box of $T$ entries. Axis $i$ has $T/t_i$ lines of cost $O(t_ip^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$. Errors and times add over $d$ passes: error less than $dp^2$, time $O(dTp^{3/2+\delta}\alpha)$ with a constant independent of $d$.

For a unit $c$ modulo $q$, let $(R_cz)_j=z_{cj}$. Substituting $h=ck$ in the Fourier sum gives $F_q^+R_c=R_c^{-1}F_q^+$. Each $t_i$ is a unit modulo $s_i$, so tensoring gives $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+$. A permutation commutes with pointwise products, so the left side is $RF_{\boldsymbol s}^+R(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\cdot F_{\boldsymbol s}v)=F_{\boldsymbol s}^+(F_{\boldsymbol s}u\cdot F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$. The normalized convolution rule is $F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=S(F_{\boldsymbol s}u)\cdot(F_{\boldsymbol s}v)$ and $F_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}=I/S$, so this equals $\frac1SF_{\boldsymbol s}^+F_{\boldsymbol s}(u*v)=u*v/S^2$.

relations.quote: Each prime-length transform is computed through a power-of-two one by [Gaussian resampling](gaussian-resampling.md).

The target permutation $Q$ is absorbed by the [Bluestein chirp identity](chirp.md), which for even $t_i$ and $a_{\boldsymbol j}=\exp(-\pi i\sum_is_ij_i^2/t_i)$ gives $QF_{\boldsymbol t}u=\overline a\cdot\bigl(a*(\overline a\cdot u)\bigr)/T$, with $*$ the [cyclic convolution](convolution.md) and a dot coordinatewise multiplication.
